answer: Each identity runs one walnut bay, locks a 70-credit bond, and files one signed stock-turn record per epoch. Crates appear on an echo board; each outbound crate carries a raven seal recorded once. Audit recomputes stock: inbound minus outbound must match the filed stock; a reused raven seal or missing crate burns the bond. The first bay costs 22; the k-th fake pays 22+5(k-1), the 1000th 5017, so 1000 fakes pay 2,519,500 plus 70,000 at risk. A rented-bay ring fails: receipts are key-bound to the owner, one record per bay per epoch. An honest keeper pays 22 once and keeps the bond.
